history.contentIn: The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was a scientific initiative proposed by Harvard University aimed solely at understanding the behavior of aerosol particles in the stratosphere. Led by Frank Keutsch and his team, this project was not about deploying geoengineering or cooling the planet; rather, it sought to enhance our computer models that assess the potential risks and benefits associated with solar geoengineering. A planned hardware test in Sweden in 2021 was intended to gauge the platform's capabilities without releasing any particles, emphasizing the need for public engagement and accountability before any further steps could be taken. In March 2024, Harvard decided to discontinue the SCoPEx project, redirecting the platform towards other stratospheric research. This decision underscores the importance of transparency and justice in climate science, reminding us that our focus must remain on meaningful mitigation efforts and equity in tackling climate change, rather than relying on unproven and potentially dangerous geoengineering solutions.
